I have an idea how to improve the code - how can I share it?

Amazing, I'm so happy that you took your time to go through the code and want to make it better!

  • If you have an idea (but no solution yet), feel free to open an issue or reach out to Cosima.
  • If you have an idea and a solution - amazing! Let's work together with PRs 😊
How to collaborate on a code level?

To allow dependency management, this repository uses uv and pre-commit hooks. To get started, there's not a lot you have to do. Just follow these steps:

  1. Install uv. See the uv installation guide for options.
  2. Now you're good to go. pyproject.toml contains all relevant info. You just need to run uv sync in your terminal. This will create a .venv/ folder with the Python packages installed in.
  3. If you want to add a package, don't do it manually. Run uv add <package_name>.
  4. This repository also relies on pre-commit hooks. To have them activated on your end, make sure to run uv run pre-commit install. They'll be running in the background and just complain if something's not right. Otherwise, you'll not really see them 😊

In case you run into issues here, let me know! We'll figure it out 😊

What's the default branch?

The default branch is main. To contribute to it, create a feature branch and open a PR with your changes. Direct pushes to main are blocked (because that's where our production code is) but collaboration is of course highly welcome 😊

Any other open questions?

If you have any questions or suggestions, please reach out to Cosima or open an issue.

docs.title: Debugging locally with debug.py
docs.text: debug.py is the single entry point for running any bot module locally. It lets you verify that a module connects correctly, reads the right data, and would post the right content — without touching any live account unless you explicitly flip the live-run flag.

docs.title: Quick start (for experienced contributors)
docs.text:
Already familiar with the setup? Here's the short path:

  1. Add credentials for your target bot/platform to .env in the project root.
  2. Open src/debug.py and edit the four knobs in DebugBots.__init__:
self.bot           = 'pyladies'   # 'pyladies' or 'rladies'
self.what_to_debug = 'blog'       # 'blog' | 'rss' | 'boost_tags' | 'boost_mentions' | 'anniversary' | 'packages' | 'package'
self.platform      = 'bluesky'    # 'bluesky' or 'mastodon'
self.no_dry_run    = False        # False = safe dry run, True = actually post
  1. Run from the project root:
uv run python src/debug.py
  1. Check the INFO log output. When everything looks right, switch no_dry_run = True and run again.

Always start with no_dry_run = False. The dry-run path logs everything the bot would do without writing any data or posting anything.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
debug.py exposes four settings that control what runs and how:

Knob Values Effect bot 'pyladies' | 'rladies' Which community's credentials and config to use what_to_debug see Scenario reference Which bot module to exercise platform 'bluesky' | 'mastodon' Which platform to connect to (ignored by rss) no_dry_run False (default) | True False = log-only, True = live API calls

docs.title: 1. Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.12
  • uv: see the uv installation guide
  • Project dependencies: uv sync

docs.title: 2. Create a .env file
docs.text:
Create a file named .env in the project root. You only need the variables for the bot/platform combination you are testing — see each scenario below for the exact keys required.

# --- Bluesky credentials ---
PYLADIES_BSKY_USERNAME=your-handle.bsky.social
PYLADIES_BSKY_PASSWORD=your-app-password        # must be an app password, not your login password

RLADIES_BSKY_USERNAME=your-handle.bsky.social
RLADIES_BSKY_PASSWORD=your-app-password

# --- Mastodon credentials ---
PYLADIES_MASTODON_USERNAME=your-username
PYLADIES_MASTODON_PASSWORD=your-password
PYLADIES_MASTODON_ACCESS_TOKEN=your-access-token
PYLADIES_BOT_CLIENTCRED_SECRET=path/to/pyladies.secret

RLADIES_MASTODON_USERNAME=your-username
RLADIES_MASTODON_PASSWORD=your-password
RLADIES_MASTODON_ACCESS_TOKEN=your-access-token
RLADIES_BOT_CLIENTCRED_SECRET=path/to/rladies.secret

# --- AI summaries (blog scenario only) ---
GEMINI_API_KEY=your-gemini-key

Bluesky: use an app password (Bluesky Settings → Privacy & Security → App Passwords), not your main account password.

Mastodon: the access token must have read and write:statuses scopes. Re-generate it in your Mastodon account settings if in doubt.

docs.title: Preferred: uv (from the project root)
docs.text:
uv run python src/debug.py

uv resolves the virtualenv and dependencies automatically — no cd src or manual environment activation needed.

docs.title: Alternative: VS Code debugger
docs.text:
Add a launch configuration to .vscode/launch.json:

{
    "version": "0.2.0",
    "configurations": [
        {
            "name": "Debug bot (uv)",
            "type": "debugpy",
            "request": "launch",
            "program": "${workspaceFolder}/src/debug.py",
            "python": "${workspaceFolder}/.venv/bin/python",
            "cwd": "${workspaceFolder}/src",
            "envFile": "${workspaceFolder}/.env",
            "preLaunchTask": "Check requirements"
        }
    ]
}

And the corresponding tasks.json:

{
    "version": "2.0.0",
    "tasks": [
        {
            "label": "Check requirements",
            "type": "shell",
            "command": "uv sync"
        }
    ]
}

This lets you set breakpoints in any bot module and step through execution. The cwd is set to src/ so relative imports resolve correctly, and .env is loaded automatically.

docs.title: Scenario reference
docs.text:
The table below summarises all seven scenarios at a glance, showing what each exercises and whether credentials or a platform selection are required.

what_to_debug What it exercises Needs credentials? Platform matters? blog Fetch RSS → check archive → (post) blog entry Yes Yes rss Fetch blog list from GitHub → update local JSON No No boost_tags Search posts by hashtag → (boost) matching posts Yes Yes boost_mentions Fetch mentions → (boost/repost) them Yes Yes anniversary Read events.json → (post) today's anniversary Yes Yes packages Fetch package list from GitHub → update local JSON No No package Read package metadata → check version → (post) next package Yes Yes

docs.title: Scenario 1 — blog: promote a blog post
docs.text: Goal: Verify that the bot can read the RSS feed, find posts not yet in the archive, build a correctly formatted post, and (in live mode) publish it.

docs.title: When to use this
docs.text:
• After changing promote_blog_post.py or the post-building logic
  • When testing a new bot/platform combination for the first time
  • When the archive or counter file is suspected to be out of sync

docs.title: Required env vars
docs.text:
The required environment variables depend on the bot and platform combination you are testing.

Combination Vars needed pyladies + bluesky PYLADIES_BSKY_USERNAME, PYLADIES_BSKY_PASSWORD, GEMINI_API_KEY pyladies + mastodon PYLADIES_MASTODON_USERNAME, PYLADIES_MASTODON_PASSWORD, PYLADIES_MASTODON_ACCESS_TOKEN, PYLADIES_BOT_CLIENTCRED_SECRET, GEMINI_API_KEY rladies + bluesky RLADIES_BSKY_USERNAME, RLADIES_BSKY_PASSWORD, GEMINI_API_KEY rladies + mastodon RLADIES_MASTODON_USERNAME, RLADIES_MASTODON_PASSWORD, RLADIES_MASTODON_ACCESS_TOKEN, RLADIES_BOT_CLIENTCRED_SECRET, GEMINI_API_KEY

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Set the knobs in src/debug.py:
self.bot           = 'pyladies'   # or 'rladies'
self.what_to_debug = 'blog'
self.platform      = 'bluesky'    # or 'mastodon'
self.no_dry_run    = False
  1. Run:
uv run python src/debug.py
  1. Read the log output. A dry run shows lines like:
INFO  Initializing pyladies_bot Bot
INFO  > Connecting to bluesky
INFO  [DRY RUN] Would post: 'How I built my first R package' from https://...
  1. If the output looks correct, switch to live mode and run again:
self.no_dry_run = True

docs.title: What to watch for
docs.text:
• [DRY RUN] Would post — a new entry was found in the feed and is not yet in the archive. Good.
  • Archive is up to date with the feed — every entry in the RSS feed is already archived. If you just reset the archive file, the feed itself may not have changed.
  • No config for bot=… platform=… — your bot/platform combination is not supported. Check the values.

docs.title: Files read/written
docs.text:
File Purpose metadata/pyladies_meta_data.json (or rladies) Blog feed index — lists all known feeds metadata/pyladies_counter_bluesky.txt (or variant) Counter tracking which feed was last processed pyladies_archive_directory_bluesky/file.json (or variant) Archive of already-posted links

The archive is only written to disk if no_dry_run = True and a post is sent successfully.

docs.title: Scenario 2 — rss: update the blog feed index
docs.text: Goal: Verify that the bot can reach the GitHub repository that lists community blogs, parse the blog entries, and write an updated JSON metadata file locally.

docs.title: When to use this
docs.text:
• After a new blog is added to the awesome-pyladies-blogs or awesome-rladies-blogs repository
  • When the metadata JSON file is suspected to be stale or missing

docs.title: Required env vars
docs.text: None — this scenario reads from public GitHub URLs only.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Set the knobs:
self.bot           = 'pyladies'   # or 'rladies'
self.what_to_debug = 'rss'
self.platform      = 'bluesky'    # value is ignored for this scenario
self.no_dry_run    = False
  1. Run:
uv run python src/debug.py
  1. Inspect metadata/pyladies_meta_data.json (or rladies) to confirm it was updated.

docs.title: What to watch for
docs.text:
• The log should show each blog entry being fetched.
  • A network error means the public GitHub URL is unreachable — check your internet connection or whether the repository has moved.
  • no_dry_run has no meaningful effect here — the metadata JSON is always written when the fetch succeeds, because the RSS fetch is a read-only operation from the platform's perspective.

docs.title: Scenario 3 — boost_tags: boost posts by hashtag
docs.text: Goal: Verify that the bot can search the platform for posts tagged with the community hashtag (#pyladies or #rladies), identify unboosted ones, and (in live mode) boost or repost them.

docs.title: When to use this
docs.text:
• After changing boost_tags.py
  • When investigating why the tag-boost job did or did not run

docs.title: Required env vars
docs.text:
The required environment variables depend on the bot and platform combination you are testing.

Combination Vars needed pyladies + bluesky PYLADIES_BSKY_USERNAME, PYLADIES_BSKY_PASSWORD pyladies + mastodon PYLADIES_MASTODON_USERNAME, PYLADIES_MASTODON_PASSWORD, PYLADIES_MASTODON_ACCESS_TOKEN, PYLADIES_BOT_CLIENTCRED_SECRET rladies + bluesky RLADIES_BSKY_USERNAME, RLADIES_BSKY_PASSWORD rladies + mastodon RLADIES_MASTODON_USERNAME, RLADIES_MASTODON_PASSWORD, RLADIES_MASTODON_ACCESS_TOKEN, RLADIES_BOT_CLIENTCRED_SECRET

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Set the knobs:
self.bot           = 'rladies'      # or 'pyladies'
self.what_to_debug = 'boost_tags'
self.platform      = 'mastodon'     # or 'bluesky'
self.no_dry_run    = False
  1. Run:
uv run python src/debug.py

  1. The log shows posts found under the hashtag and whether each would be boosted or skipped.

  2. If the output looks right, set no_dry_run = True and run again.

docs.title: What to watch for
docs.text:
• [DRY RUN] Would boost — a new post was found and would be boosted. Good.
  • No boost lines at all — no recent posts under that hashtag, or all recent ones have already been boosted. This is normal.
  • A login error almost always means the credentials in .env are wrong or the app password has been revoked.

docs.title: Scenario 4 — boost_mentions: boost posts that mention the bot
docs.text: Goal: Verify that the bot can fetch its notification feed, identify new mentions, and (in live mode) boost or repost them.

docs.title: When to use this
docs.text:
• After changing boost_mentions.py
  • When investigating why a mention was not boosted

docs.title: Required env vars
docs.text: Same as boost_tags — see the table in Scenario 3.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Set the knobs:
self.bot           = 'rladies'         # or 'pyladies'
self.what_to_debug = 'boost_mentions'
self.platform      = 'bluesky'         # or 'mastodon'
self.no_dry_run    = False
  1. Run:
uv run python src/debug.py

  1. The log shows each notification and whether it would be boosted or skipped.

  2. If the output looks right, set no_dry_run = True and run again.

docs.title: What to watch for
docs.text:
• [DRY RUN] Would boost toot by … (Mastodon) or [DRY RUN] Would repost URI … (Bluesky) — a new mention was found and would be acted on.
  • Successfully processed notifications. Last seen at: … — the Bluesky notification cursor was updated (live mode only).
  • A mention is silently skipped if it was already reblogged by the bot, or if it came from the bot account itself — both are correct behaviour.

docs.title: Scenario 5 — anniversary: post a community anniversary
docs.text: Goal: Verify that the bot reads metadata/events.json, finds any event matching today's date (MM-DD), builds a correctly formatted post, and (in live mode) sends it with the correct image.

docs.title: When to use this
docs.text:
• After changing promote_anniversaries.py
  • After adding or editing an entry in metadata/events.json
  • When you want to test the image-upload path

docs.title: Required env vars
docs.text:
The required environment variables depend on the bot and platform combination you are testing.

Combination Vars needed pyladies + bluesky PYLADIES_BSKY_USERNAME, PYLADIES_BSKY_PASSWORD pyladies + mastodon PYLADIES_MASTODON_USERNAME, PYLADIES_MASTODON_PASSWORD, PYLADIES_MASTODON_ACCESS_TOKEN, PYLADIES_BOT_CLIENTCRED_SECRET rladies + bluesky RLADIES_BSKY_USERNAME, RLADIES_BSKY_PASSWORD rladies + mastodon RLADIES_MASTODON_USERNAME, RLADIES_MASTODON_PASSWORD, RLADIES_MASTODON_ACCESS_TOKEN, RLADIES_BOT_CLIENTCRED_SECRET

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Prepare a test event. Open metadata/events.json and confirm at least one entry has today's date in MM-DD format:
{
  "name": "Ada Lovelace",
  "date": "12-10",
  "description_mastodon": "...",
  "description_bluesky": "...",
  "wiki_link": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ada_Lovelace",
  "bluesky": "@ada.bsky.social",
  "img": "ada_lovelace.png",
  "alt": "Portrait of Ada Lovelace"
}

If no entry matches today, temporarily add one with today's date. Do not commit that change — it's for local testing only.

  1. Set the knobs:
self.bot           = 'pyladies'      # or 'rladies'
self.what_to_debug = 'anniversary'
self.platform      = 'bluesky'       # or 'mastodon'
self.no_dry_run    = False
  1. Run:
uv run python src/debug.py
  1. The log shows:
INFO  [DRY RUN] Would post anniversary for Ada Lovelace on 12-10
  1. If the output looks right, set no_dry_run = True and run again. The bot will download the image (if an img key is present), upload it to the platform, and send the post.

docs.title: What to watch for
docs.text:
• No anniversary output — no entry in events.json matches today's date. Add a test entry as described in step 1.
  • Image already downloaded — the image was cached locally on a previous run. Safe to ignore; the local copy will be used.
  • Media upload failed … falling back to text-only — the image could not be uploaded (network issue or unsupported format). The post still goes out without the image, and the exception is logged. Check the img path and the platform's media limits.
  • On Bluesky, the handle in the bluesky field (e.g. @ada.bsky.social) is resolved to a DID via the public API. If that lookup fails, the name is used as plain text — the post still goes out.

docs.title: Scenario 6 — packages: update the package metadata
docs.text: Goal: Verify that the bot can reach the GitHub repository that lists community packages, download each package JSON, and write an updated metadata file locally.

docs.title: When to use this
docs.text:
• After a new package is added to awesome-pyladies-creations or awesome-rladies-creations
  • When the package metadata JSON is suspected to be stale or missing
  • Before testing the package scenario

docs.title: Required env vars
docs.text: None — this scenario reads from public GitHub URLs only.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Set the knobs:
self.bot           = 'pyladies'   # or 'rladies'
self.what_to_debug = 'packages'
self.platform      = 'bluesky'    # value is ignored for this scenario
self.no_dry_run    = False
  1. Run:
uv run python src/debug.py
  1. Inspect metadata/pyladies_packages_meta_data.json (or rladies) to confirm it was updated with the expected entries.

docs.title: What to watch for
docs.text:
• The log should show each package JSON being fetched and parsed.
  • A network error means a public GitHub URL is unreachable — check your internet connection or whether the repository has moved.
  • no_dry_run = False still logs the full list of entries that would be written without touching the file. Set no_dry_run = True to actually write to disk.

docs.title: Files read/written
docs.text: File Purpose metadata/pyladies_packages_meta_data.json (or rladies) Output — package metadata used by the package bot

docs.title: Scenario 7 — package: promote a community package
docs.text: Goal: Verify that the bot can read the package metadata, determine the next package to promote (checking its version against the archive), build a correctly formatted post, and (in live mode) publish it.

docs.title: When to use this
docs.text:
• After changing promote_package.py
  • After running the packages scenario to refresh the metadata
  • When the counter or archive file is suspected to be out of sync

docs.title: Required env vars
docs.text: Combination Vars needed pyladies + bluesky PYLADIES_BSKY_USERNAME, PYLADIES_BSKY_PASSWORD pyladies + mastodon PYLADIES_MASTODON_USERNAME, PYLADIES_MASTODON_PASSWORD, PYLADIES_MASTODON_ACCESS_TOKEN, PYLADIES_BOT_CLIENTCRED_SECRET rladies + bluesky RLADIES_BSKY_USERNAME, RLADIES_BSKY_PASSWORD rladies + mastodon RLADIES_MASTODON_USERNAME, RLADIES_MASTODON_PASSWORD, RLADIES_MASTODON_ACCESS_TOKEN, RLADIES_BOT_CLIENTCRED_SECRET

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Make sure the metadata file is populated first (run the packages scenario if needed).

  2. Set the knobs:

self.bot           = 'pyladies'   # or 'rladies'
self.what_to_debug = 'package'
self.platform      = 'bluesky'    # or 'mastodon'
self.no_dry_run    = False
  1. Run:
uv run python src/debug.py
  1. Read the log output. A dry run shows the full formatted post that would be sent:
INFO  Initializing pyladies_bot Bot
INFO  > Connecting to bluesky
INFO  Considering package: CiteLang
INFO  Promoting package: CiteLang
INFO    Version: 0.1.2
INFO  [DRY RUN] Would promote: CiteLang (https://github.com/vsoch/citelang)
      📦 CiteLang

      Generate credit summaries.

      👤 Vanessa Sochat (@vsoch.bsky.social)

      🔗 https://github.com/vsoch/citelang

      #pyladies #python #opensource
  1. If the output looks correct, switch to live mode and run again:
self.no_dry_run = True

docs.title: What to watch for
docs.text:
• [DRY RUN] Would promote: … — a package was found that is either new or has a newer version. The full post text is shown. Good.
  • Skipping … — already promoted at version … — the package is already in the archive at its current version. The bot will try the next package in the list.
  • All packages already promoted at their current version — nothing to post — every package is up to date. Use this to confirm the archive is working correctly. To force a re-run, delete the relevant entry from the archive JSON.
  • ARCHIVE_FILE not configured — the archive_file key is missing from the config. Version tracking is disabled; all packages are treated as new every cycle.
  • A login error almost always means the credentials in .env are wrong or the app password has been revoked.

docs.title: Files read/written
docs.text:
File Purpose metadata/pyladies_packages_meta_data.json (or rladies) Input — package list produced by the packages scenario metadata/pyladies_packages_counter_bluesky.txt (or variant) Tracks which package was last promoted metadata/pyladies_packages_archive.json (or rladies) Records each promoted package and its version to prevent re-promotion

The counter and archive are only written to disk if no_dry_run = True and a post is sent successfully.

docs.title: "No config for bot=… platform=…"
docs.text:
Your bot/platform combination is not in the supported matrix. Valid combinations:

bot platform pyladies bluesky pyladies mastodon rladies bluesky rladies mastodon

The rss scenario ignores platform entirely.

docs.title: Login errors
docs.text:
• Bluesky: PYLADIES_BSKY_PASSWORD / RLADIES_BSKY_PASSWORD must be an app password (Bluesky Settings → Privacy & Security → App Passwords), not your main account password.
  • Mastodon: the access token must have read and write:statuses scopes. Re-generate it in your Mastodon account settings if in doubt.

docs.title: ModuleNotFoundError / ImportError
docs.text:
Run from the project root using uv, not from inside src/:

# Correct
uv run python src/debug.py

# Wrong — relative imports break
cd src && python debug.py

docs.title: Dry run shows nothing
docs.text:
• blog: all entries in the RSS feed are already in the archive. Delete or empty the archive file (archive_directory*/file.json) to force a re-run.
  • boost_tags / boost_mentions: no recent posts match the criteria. Post something yourself on the relevant platform under the hashtag and try again.
  • anniversary: no entry in events.json matches today's date. Add a temporary test entry (see Scenario 5, step 1).
  • packages: the metadata JSON was already up to date. This is normal — run with no_dry_run = True to write (overwrite) it regardless.
  • package: every package in the metadata is already in the archive at its current version. To force a re-run, remove the relevant entry (or all entries) from metadata/pyladies_packages_archive.json (or rladies).
